description: I'm an AI and software innovation enthusiast passionate about space exploration. Our mission is to build an interactive digital museum showcasing NASA's abandoned lunar and Martian equipment through verified images, mission histories, and compelling stories. We're seeking teammates skilled in coding, AI/ML, design, data visualization, space science, research, and storytelling to create an engaging educational experience.
summary:
Space Relics: The Planetary Archaeology Atlas & Virtual Museum is an interactive educational website that explores the remains of NASA missions on the Moon and Mars. It brings together four featured relics: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module and EASEP, Surveyor 3, Sojourner from Mars Pathfinder, and the Opportunity rover.

The platform features a schematic planetary Atlas, museum-style exhibitions, interactive learning activities, and a Knowledge Centre with mission timelines, comparisons, a glossary, and research resources. Each exhibition presents the object's mission history, location, design, scientific contributions, and legacy, supported by NASA archival imagery and mission records.

By transforming scattered information about abandoned space hardware into an accessible digital museum, Space Relics addresses the challenge through research-based storytelling and interactive education. It helps students and young space enthusiasts understand that these objects are lasting records of scientific discovery, engineering achievements, and humanity's exploration beyond Earth.
details:
Space Relics is an interactive educational website that explores NASA mission remnants on the Moon and Mars. Visitors can switch between the two planetary environments using a schematic Atlas and discover four featured relics: Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, Sojourner and Opportunity.

The website includes museum-style exhibitions explaining each object's mission history, location, design, scientific discoveries and legacy. It also offers four interactive learning activities, a Knowledge Centre with timelines, comparisons and a glossary, and a personal reflection experience with a downloadable keepsake.

The project makes information about abandoned space hardware easier to explore and understand. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about planetary science, engineering and space exploration among students and young enthusiasts.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript and hosted it on Netlify. Its creative approach combines planetary archaeology, digital museum exhibitions and interactive learning to turn mission records and archival imagery into an engaging educational experience. We considered factual accuracy, accessibility, ease of navigation, responsive design and reliable research sources throughout development.
